key_description: Looping animation of step 25's cut-open bean bud: in a magnified inset a pollen grain on the stigma sends out a tube that grows down through the style, while in the main view a gold glow travels round the spiral keel to an ovule; a clock under the inset counts the hours
viewer_what: A cutaway 3D model of a plant ovary shaped like a snail shell or coiled spiral, on a green stalk. It is labeled Phaseolus vulgaris (common bean), with a 1 mm scale bar. The straight part holds a row of six white oval ovules. A circular magnified inset (x10.3, 100 um scale bar) shows the spiral's centre: a pale green ball with yellow grains on it and white hair-like projections above.
viewer_change_or_point: The caption under the inset counts up: 0 h 00, 0 h 10, 2 h 10, 5 h 40, 9 h 20, then back to 0 h 00 min 'since the tube emerged'. In the inset, a thin yellow tube is absent in frames 1 and 6. In frames 2 to 5 it runs from one yellow grain on the green ball upward toward the green column. It looks the same length in frames 2 through 5, so I cannot see it grow in the inset after frame 2. In the main view, a faint yellow line seems to spread along the coils of the spiral in frames 4 and 5, reaching toward the stalk that leads to the ovules. It is subtle and hard to follow at this size. The rest of the model does not move. A dotted leader labeled 'the same ovary, ~14 days later' points at a blurry green smudge below the model. That smudge looks the same in every frame, and I cannot make out any object in it.
viewer_where: The magnified circle at upper right and the time caption under it, then the coiled spiral in the main model, where the faint yellow line appears.

key_description: A gold-plated padlock lying on its back on a grey table, its front face mirroring a softbox in pale gold; an inset cuts through the surface to show 0.5 µm of gold over 3 µm of nickel over brass, beside a dashed circle the width of a cotton fibre, and a chart shows gold's reflectance rising steeply above 500 nm while silver's stays flat
viewer_what: A 3D render of a gold-plated padlock titled 'A gold-plated padlock', with a magnified cross-section panel and a reflectance graph beside it.
viewer_change_or_point: It explains why the lock looks gold. The text says the colour was not picked but computed from gold's measured optical constants. The cross-section, drawn true to scale, shows a very thin 0.5 um gold layer over 3 um of nickel over the brass body, next to a 15 um cotton fibre for scale, so the gold is thinner than the fibre is wide. The graph shows silver reflecting nearly 100% across the visible spectrum. Gold reflects only about 40% below about 508 nm (2.4 eV), so it absorbs blue and looks yellow.
viewer_where: The small circle on the lock's front face, and the cross-section panel at right that it zooms into, especially the thin gold stripe. Then the reflectance graph at lower right.
